messages:
pagerduty-bot: PAGER: High tail latency detected for CrescentBank (dedicated-pool-eu2). p95=820ms p99=1870ms sustained 10m. Alert: PD-46288. Affected endpoints: /v1/chat (stream), /v1/completions.
sara.l: oncall here, joining. any customer message yet? :rotating_light:
tom.b: infra investigating node-level anomalies. saw intermittent nvme latency on host eu2-node-14 around 04:10 UTC.
eng-runtime: noted. No runtime deploys in last 8h. We do have a spike in long scheduler wait times for tenant `ad-hoc-reports`.
sre-oncall: errors are low (0.1%) but tail is nasty. Paging customer-eng to let CrescentBank know.
ops-bot: War room created: #INC-CrescentBank-eu2-tail. Link: https://redwood/warrooms/INC-46288
evans-c: Hi all, CrescentBank engineering (contact: maya/crescent) is on standby. They report intermittent UI hangs, not full failures. Asking if you can rollback anything.
sara.l: no user deploys. this looks infra/runtime. tom, can you paste nvme latencies?
tom.b: logs: ```
[2026-03-15T04:08:59Z] eu2-node-14 nvme_latency_ms=6
[2026-03-15T04:10:12Z] eu2-node-14 nvme_latency_ms=420
[2026-03-15T04:10:58Z] eu2-node-14 nvme_latency_ms=900  <-- heavy tail
[2026-03-15T04:11:22Z] eu2-node-16 nvme_latency_ms=8
[2026-03-15T04:12:05Z] eu2-node-14 kernel_sched_wait_ms=320
```
eng-runtime: correlating that with scheduler logs: host eu2-node-14 shows GPU driver stall events causing host-side batching to block ~800ms. Looks like a storage-induced I/O stall.
sre-oncall: can we evict the noisy tenant `ad-hoc-reports` from eu2-node-14? We have per-tenant fairness.
infra: we can cordon eu2-node-14 and drain pods, but draining will cause transient scheduling which might spike latency momentarily. Suggest: 1) route CrescentBank to `eu2-warm-fallback` for sensitive traffic (low-latency mode), 2) cordon+reprovision node eu2-node-14, 3) migrate noisy tenant to `batch-eu2` isolated pool.
eng-runtime: we also have an option to switch CrescentBank model endpoint to a lighter quantized variant `gptx-small-q4` which reduces token-latency by ~35% for identical sequences. That could be a fast mitigation while infra works. Command for quick model fallback: `rb model route-set --customer crescentbank --model gptx-small-q4 --ttl 1800`
sara.l: agree: do model fallback + route to warm-fallback for streaming. evan, can you notify customer about temporary model fallback and possible minor quality difference?
evans-c: notifying now. CrescentBank ok with short-lived fallback as long as performance returns. Maya asks for ETA ~30m.
sara.l: executing model fallback now.
eng-runtime: output: ```
> rb model route-set --customer crescentbank --model gptx-small-q4 --ttl 1800
Applied. New model variant active: 04:14:03 UTC
```
ops-bot: Canary check: 3/3 canary hosts reporting decreased latency for the route.
sre-oncall: after fallback, p99 dropped from 1870ms -> 520ms in ~25s. p95 ~180ms. Customer impact reduced.
tom.b: cordoning eu2-node-14 now: `kubectl cordon eu2-node-14` -> OK. Starting drain.
infra: drain logs: ```
Draining eu2-node-14: removing 8 pods. evicted: tenant=ad-hoc-reports (4 pods), tenant=analytics (2 pods), system (2 pods)
Rebalance started to eu2-node-15/16/18
Host reprovision job started: REPRO-1122
```
eng-runtime: while migrating, we saw 2x kv-cache miss rate on ad-hoc-reports tenant which aligns with batch loads hitting storage. We'll prioritize placing that tenant on `batch-eu2` with isolated NVMe-backed pool. Command: `rb tenant migrate ad-hoc-reports --to batch-eu2 --drain 60`
sara.l: please schedule migration; prefer graceful drain to avoid extra tail for other customers.
infra: migration kicked: JOB MIG-99202. Estimated migrate time ~9m.
evans-c: CrescentBank reports responsiveness improving after fallback. will continue to monitor.
karen.t: quick note: we should be careful with automatic tenant placement; consider adding NVMe health as a scheduling affinity so heavy IO tenants don't land on shared latency-sensitive hosts. Adding as follow-up.
sre-oncall: monitoring: p99 back to ~460ms at 04:20 UTC, trending stable. No significant error spike.
eng-runtime: MIG-99202 completed at 04:23:15 UTC. ad-hoc-reports moved to batch-eu2. Node reprovision REPRO-1122 finished 04:27:02 UTC.
sara.l: rolling back model fallback? Customer quality matters; wait until settings stable. Recommend keep fallback for 30m then revert if stable.
evans-c: CrescentBank agrees to 30m hold. They appreciate the gradation approach.
sre-oncall: remediation summary: model fallback + warm-fallback route + node cordon+drain + tenant migration. Latency returned to baseline in ~12m from first page.
eng-runtime: follow-ups: 1) schedule scheduler affinity change for NVMe-latency tagging (eng-runtime + infra) 2) run regular NVMe health audit for eu2 3) postmortem/incident writeup (sara.l owner) 4) consider adding rapid model-fallback runbook in playbooks.
sara.l: owners assigned: sara.l -> postmortem draft; tom.b -> reprovisioning and NVMe audit; eng-runtime -> affinity + runbook; evan-c -> customer note.
ops-bot: War room closed by sara.l at 04:29 UTC. Keep monitoring for 1h.
sre-oncall: handing back to normal ops; if p99 > 800ms or errors > 1% reopen.
evans-c: CrescentBank: thanks for fast mitigation. Please include details on how fallback affects output quality.
sara.l: will include in customer note. Great job team. :thumbsup:
eng-runtime: adding issue to backlog for model-fallback automation for future incidents.
